text:
The Mammoth's season has a goaltending subplot. Sebastian Cossa has taken over the starting job from Karel Vejmelka, who has won just one of his last nine starts, and Cossa started the two wins that ended a six-game losing streak, per The Hockey News. Monday's 4-2 loss in Winnipeg kept the crease the question.

Everything in front of it looks like a playoff team. Utah has 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 57% at 5-on-5, but it's 12-10-3, about four points short of what its play has earned by our standings model. The gap is mostly in net: the Mammoth have allowed about 10.6 more goals than their chances against predict.

Logan Cooley is the engine, with 15 points in his last 10 games against 10.6 expected. Jack McBain fought Gabriel Landeskog in what USA Today called a revenge fight, and Liam O'Brien told the Denver Post, "If you touch any of our top guys, me and the boys are coming for you." Dylan Guenther is off injured reserve but sat out Monday.

The Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton line takes 74% of the expected goals at 5-on-5. MacKenzie Weegar and Mikhail Sergachev win 56% of the chances yet have been on for 6 goals for and 14 against, the clearest place better saves would show up.

Our playoff odds have Utah at 65%. What we'd watch: how many starts in a row Cossa gets.
headline: Utah wins the chances, and Cossa takes the crease
